about: The character controls of WindCore: what a player would call them, the model setting each one moves, and what was measured when it moves. Every control runs 0 to 1. An interface can be generated from this file.

groups.label: Player
groups.hint: What the person does: mouth shape, embouchure, air.

groups.label: Mouthpiece and reed
groups.hint: What is in the mouth: reed, chamber, baffle.

groups.label: Horn
groups.hint: The tube: cone, tone holes, bell.

groups.label: Life
groups.hint: What the player's body does to a held note. All at zero is a perfectly still player.

controls.label: Mouth shape
controls.display: two resonance markers on a spectrum, fixed in Hz, sliding as the vowel changes
controls.says: The vowel the mouth makes, heard as two resonances that stay at the same frequencies whatever the note: oo at one end, ah in the middle, ee at the other. It can be played while holding a note.
controls.basis: A filter on the radiated sound, not a tract model: the physical tract upstream of the reed made no formant in this model. Li, Chen, Smith, Wolfe 2015 report 5-10 dB near a tuned tract resonance.

controls.label: Mouth strength
controls.display: height of the same markers
controls.says: How strongly that vowel colours the sound, up to 10 dB at its upper resonance. At 0 the mouth is neutral. It does not change tuning.
controls.basis: Li, Chen, Smith, Wolfe 2015 (several harmonics moved 5-10 dB by expert players, much less by others)

controls.label: Embouchure
controls.display: reed tip gap
controls.says: How open the reed tip is held. Looser is louder and brighter, tighter is smaller and darker.
controls.basis: Wilson, Beavers 1974; Dalmont, Gilbert, Ollivier 2003

controls.label: Air
controls.display: noise floor under the harmonics
controls.says: Turbulence in the air stream past the reed. It rides on the flow, so it pulses with each cycle and is heard through the horn, not laid on top.
controls.basis: Scavone 1996 (turbulent flow at the reed)

controls.label: Reed
controls.display: reed closing curve
controls.says: How abruptly the reed closes against the mouthpiece. A soft, gradual closing rounds the tone, an abrupt one adds edge.
controls.basis: Avanzini, van Walstijn 2004 (reed bending on the lay)

controls.label: Chamber
controls.display: mouthpiece cross-section
controls.says: The volume inside the mouthpiece, which stands in for the missing tip of the cone. Large is darker and more spread, small is tighter and more focused. Well below this range the low notes jump to their octave.
controls.basis: Benade 1976; Kergomard et al. 2019

controls.label: Baffle
controls.display: mouthpiece cross-section
controls.says: How far up the spectrum the chamber keeps absorbing. A high baffle lets the upper harmonics through: more buzz and cut.
controls.basis: A simplification of ours: the chamber as a volume behind a resistance

controls.label: Cone
controls.unit: share of the cone that is missing
controls.display: waveform: share of the cycle the reed is closed
controls.says: How much of the cone is cut off at the top. It sets how long the reed stays closed in each cycle, and so which harmonics are hollowed out: near 0.33 the third is weak, toward 0.5 the even ones go, as on a clarinet.
controls.basis: Dalmont, Gilbert, Kergomard 2000; Kergomard et al. 2019

controls.label: Tone holes
controls.display: cutoff line on a spectrum
controls.says: The frequency above which sound leaves through the open holes instead of travelling back up the horn. Higher gives more ringing upper harmonics and a little less level.
controls.basis: Benade 1976 (tone-hole lattice cutoff)

controls.label: Bell
controls.display: tilt on a spectrum
controls.says: A plain tilt of the radiated sound. It changes nothing in how the horn plays.
controls.basis: None: an equaliser

controls.label: Body
controls.display: fixed peaks and dips on a spectrum, staying put as notes move
controls.says: Peaks and dips that stay at the same frequencies whatever the note: a hump near 450 Hz, a dip near 800 Hz, humps from 1.6 to 3 kHz, less above 5 kHz. Every collected saxophone has such a pattern; without it this model had less than any of them.
controls.basis: Measured on the collected sources (tools/body.py); Kergomard et al. 2019 (fixed anti-formants of conical reed instruments)

controls.label: Body size
controls.display: the same pattern sliding down or up
controls.says: Slides the whole body pattern down (a larger body) or up (a smaller one). It already moves with the range: lower for baritone notes, higher for alto and soprano notes.
controls.basis: Kergomard et al. 2019 (the pattern scales with the missing cone's length)

controls.label: Fingers
controls.display: two bore lengths crossfading
controls.says: How long a key takes to open or close in a slur. During that time the horn has two lengths at once, as with a half-open hole.
controls.basis: Hofmann, Goebl 2014 (finger actions dominate timing)

controls.label: Tongue
controls.display: attack envelope
controls.says: How fast the tongue leaves the reed at the start of a tongued note.
controls.basis: Li, Almeida, Smith, Wolfe 2016; Pamies-Vila et al. 2019

controls.label: Wobble
controls.display: level trace of a held note
controls.says: Slow random movement of the breath, so a held note's level never sits still. The collected saxophones move about 1.4 dB within a note; this model moved 0.2.
controls.basis: Measured on the collected sources; Ramirez et al. 2007 (amplitude deviations identify players)

controls.label: Shimmer
controls.display: harmonics of a held note over time
controls.says: Slow random movement of the embouchure, so the balance of harmonics shifts a little on its own, apart from loudness.
controls.basis: Measured on the collected sources

controls.label: Pitch drift
controls.display: pitch trace of a held note
controls.says: Slow random movement of pitch, a few cents either way.
controls.basis: Abesser et al. 2015 (intonation within 25 cents, personal)

controls.label: Vibrato
controls.display: pitch trace of a held note
controls.says: Vibrato that grows in after a note has been held a quarter of a second. Turn it off if you play your own.
controls.basis: Abesser et al. 2015 (about 25 cents, up to 35-50 for some players); Gilbert, Simon, Terroir 2005

controls.label: Vibrato rate
controls.display: pitch trace of a held note
controls.says: How fast the vibrato turns. Rate is a personal trait: it does not follow pitch or tempo.
controls.basis: Abesser et al. 2015

controls.label: Slur
controls.display: level trace across a note change
controls.says: How much the breath gives for a moment when the fingers move in a slur. The collected saxophones dip about 4 dB at a slurred note change; this model dipped 0.2.
controls.basis: Measured on the collected sources; Hofmann, Goebl 2014
